plate_identification.A: Left: eight stock plain fin walls under the bottom annulus

common_recipe: Production material recipe; native bridge flow 1.0, effective Bridge feed 25 mm/s, native layer-time cooling; accepted base Rx -15 degrees

photo_observations.observation: A hanging loop and multiple long loose strands are visible beneath/across the lever-facing straight rim region on the left fin-supported specimen.
The visible fin walls remain upright and their feet appear on the bed in these views. No fallen wall or obvious broad bed lift is visible.
The right tree-supported specimen is visible with distributed support contacts. The views do not expose its complete underside or establish a post-removal rim result.

native_path_evidence.lower_bearing: No lower deposited bead beneath the selected strand in its three preceding nominal courses
native_path_evidence.interpretation: The recorded native gap agrees with Derek’s front-failure attribution. Finished photographs and his direct report establish sag; the initiating deposition sequence and quantitative deflection remain unmeasured.

disposition: Completed specimens removed and compared by Derek. Stock fins do not pass the critical front appearance comparison. Easy fin release and generally uniform sagged underside are retained as separate physical results.
physical_assessment_pending: Quantified sag depth and removal force
Mating fit against the existing mounting plate
in_progress_operator_quote: What are we starting next on mark2? Here’s how its current print is failing as anticipated.
operator_quote:
Mark2 results. On the surface that matters the fins were strictly worse, simply because of that missing support in the front.

But other than that, fins worked great, lots of things did print okay, that I was worried about. Fins snapped off easy. Surface overall pretty uniform on bottom face. Sagging clearly. I think speed and cooling will help. I’m less certain how many supports we really need, because of this, perhaps we get by with less.

completed_part_results.photograph_identification: Finished photographs carry no visible specimen labels. Plate-left A and plate-right B are launch coordinates and are not applied to the post-removal arrangement.

finished_photo_observations.observation: The right article in the paired underside views has loose strands across the front of the large opening and curled perimeter strands. The left article has a more continuous front region.
finished_photo_observations.identification_limit: The right article is consistent with A’s reported front failure; this is inferred from the failure pattern, not a visible specimen label.

finished_photo_observations.observation: The oblique edge views show material hanging below the nominal face, including loops and an uneven lower edge. The views support a sag observation but do not quantify its depth.
finished_photo_observations.identification_limit: No specimen label is visible in these views.

interpretation.supported: The critical front result and easy stock-fin release are direct physical observations. The known missing native bearing at the lever-facing strand agrees with the reported location.
interpretation.support_density: This result does not establish a required fin count. A sparser layout with deliberate front contacts remains a candidate; the dense Full-mode layout is a coverage comparison, not a selected minimum.
interpretation.recipe: Derek expects speed and cooling to improve the sag. This production-recipe result does not measure that improvement.
interpretation.release_scope: Easy release applies to the eight stock walls. The 34 Full-mode walls plus three local walls on Mark1 have a separate removal result pending.
